Synopsis:
The UN and UK government are raising alarms over an unprecedented El Niño event, potentially the largest in 1,000 years, with ocean temperatures already 2.6°C above the 30-year average and forecast to peak at ~4°C anomaly in November. The UK government is preparing a public resilience campaign urging households to stockpile supplies ahead of an expected wet, stormy winter. Globally, the event threatens wildfires, floods, food insecurity (~50M people at acute hunger risk), and will compound already accelerating climate-driven extreme weather. The UK is responding with new infrastructure (reservoir construction) and farming adaptation programmes.

The pattern is structural, global in reach, and compounded by baseline global heating — highly persistent and critical.)

Severity score: 55
(Disruptions to power and water infrastructure are explicitly flagged as risks requiring household preparation. Storm/flood events in winter can damage grid infrastructure and constrain supply. Increased heating demand from a stormy, wet winter is implicitly relevant. No direct energy market language, but the supply-side risk from extreme weather events on infrastructure is real and implied.)
